K02-K03 preserve reserve readiness without letting it leak into the occupied line while root/support load changes
K04 is a one-tick authored release wedge: lead geometry physically clears upward before reserve admission

K05 spends the one-tick reserve crossing bridge inside the vacated line rather than teleporting straight to full extension

direction.problem: Two task channels share one physical line. The reserve can be visibly ready while still causally inadmissible. The lead must release the occupied line before the reserve spends its action clock.
direction.why_source_earns_problem: The commissioned whole-source evidence establishes dual-tool context plus materially different compact, extended and compressed tool relationships, while providing no reliable source-authentic timing. That makes line occupancy and reserve admission an authored timing problem rather than an observed cadence claim.

pocket_rule: READY IS NOT ADMITTED. KEEP THE RESERVE OUT OF AN OCCUPIED LINE; LET RELEASE OPEN THE WINDOW, THEN SPEND IT.

history.correction: Make K05 the one-tick authored reserve crossing bridge in the newly vacated line; defer full extension/consequence to K06 while preserving lead-high clearance and right-catch support.
history.highest_value_visible_defect: K04→K05 made the reserve jump from left-side coil directly to full rightward extension, so the release gate read but the reserve's actual crossing of the vacated line was under-authored.

history.visible_read: Lead visibly owns the shared line through bind/load; K04 physically clears the lead upward; K05 spends a short authored reserve crossing bridge only after release; K06 completes extension with right-dominant consequence; K07-K08 brake/restack displaced without lead reclaim or body-clock reset.

noodle_queen.judgment: The good bit is the refusal to confuse readiness with permission. The reserve is already hungry, but the occupied line says no; the one-tick release wedge makes the next stroke feel earned rather than queued by metadata.
